acceptance.how_to_verify:
Run this one command, which compares only the weekly end-bound cases rather than the whole file:

D=packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets
diff <(git show main:$D/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it'\K[^']+") \
     <(sed -n "/^describe(.weekly custom report end bound/,/^describe(.weekly budgeted report end bound/p" $D/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | grep -oP "it'\K[^']+")

It must print nothing and exit 0. Both sides are ten-title lists and they are equal. This is deliberately scoped: the whole file holds 23 `it('` titles, and diffing the branch file in full against main's ten prints `10a11,23` plus 13 extra titles and exits 1 even on a correct implementation — that was the defect this criterion carried in v4, and no criterion here compares whole-file lists again. The right-hand sed range is matched by describe NAME, not by line number, because the inserted comment block shifts every describe by +14 (the `weekly custom report end bound` describe is at 380 on main and 394 after this change). The range ends at the `describe` line itself, so the next describe's cases are excluded; on the applied tree this extraction yields exactly 10 titles. If a shell mangles the nested quotes, the equivalent subset form — `comm -23 <(git show main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" | sort) <(grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | sort)` — also prints nothing and exits 0; it was verified too, and is weaker (it would not notice a case added inside the two weekly describes), so prefer the diff. Separately, confirm no third file anywhere in the repo carries these titles: `git grep -l -F "it('covers the whole final week once that week has elapsed'" main -- packages` names exactly the two files being reconciled, and the same grep on the edited tree names only custom-spreadsheet.test.ts. Finally, `git diff -U0 main -- .../custom-spreadsheet.test.ts` shows no removed line, so no assertion inside the ten cases was touched.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete weekly-end-date.test.ts and move anything unique into custom-spreadsheet.test.ts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is nothing to move. The diff over the two describe blocks contains no assertion line at all, the ten titles are identical, and the bodies differ only in the props wrapper, whose defaults the shorter file already supplied. This was the epic's first option and it reduces to a plain delete.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep weekly-end-date.test.ts and delete the ten cases from custom-spreadsheet.test.ts instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It keeps the weaker of the two suites. The survivor would lose the server double that applies `$transform` precision and splits the amount filter, and it would strand the `weeklyProps` helper, which the weekly budgeted describe also uses. It also means editing a 1100-line file to delete ten cases rather than deleting a 338-line file outright.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extract the ten cases plus their fixtures and server double into a shared test helper both files import.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves both files running the same ten cases, which is the duplication the ticket exists to remove — it hides the duplication behind an import instead of ending it, and it adds a shared helper to a codebase trying to lose a file, not gain a layer.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep weekly-end-date.test.ts but mark the ten cases `it.skip`, or move them under a single shared describe imported by both.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Skipped tests still count in a reportable total, so AC-1's 'drops by exactly ten' would fail; and the shared-describe form keeps two files alive for one suite. Either leaves the 338 lines a reviewer is asked to judge, which the ticket names as half the cost.

alternatives_considered.approach: Record the comparison in both the code comment and the release note, as v1's AC-2/AC-3/qa_script step 6 required.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the objection v1 was rejected for. It cannot be carried out by the implementer: the repo's release-note convention says one sentence, and the existing precedent for a Maintenance note of this kind is a single clause with no narrative. Requiring both means the release note either violates the repo convention or fails the plan's own acceptance criteria. The obligation is therefore narrowed to the code comment.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep v2's bare repo-wide grep and add an explicit exemption list naming the comment block and the release-note filename.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the objection v2 was rejected for, and the list would be a third artefact that must be kept in step with files[1] and AC-2 — the same failure mode a third time. Scoping the grep by file type makes the two required mentions invisible to the check by construction, so there is nothing to keep in step.

alternatives_considered.approach: Take the reviewer's alternative on the comment text: drop the 'exactly the text supplied' clause from files[1] and rewrite AC-2 to require only the content, without pinning an opening phrase.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the disagreement but leaves the implementer choosing the wording, which is a judgement call the planner exists to remove — and AC-2 would then be judged by a QA agent with no memory of the implementer's reasoning. Quoting the block in full costs 13 lines and makes both artefacts point at one text.

alternatives_considered.approach: Rewrite files[1]'s comment block so the token falls on its fourth line, leaving v3's AC-2 ordinal as written.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer's required fix was explicit that the block must not be edited to chase the ordinal, because the block is the artefact AC-2 is judged against for the character-for-character match. Reordering the block to satisfy an ordinal would also read as fitting the prose to the checker. AC-2 was corrected to say third line instead, and files[1] quotes a block whose third line it is.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix AC-4 and qa_script step 2 with the reviewer's SECOND option — keep the whole-file extraction and state the real relation as a subset check, `comm -23 <(main titles | sort) <(branch titles | sort)` printing nothing.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works and was verified on the applied tree, but it is one-sided: it proves every title from main survived into the survivor and says nothing about the survivor's own two weekly describes, so a case added or renamed there would pass. The reviewer's first option — scope to the two describes and diff the two ten-title lists — fails in both directions and also keeps the check's stated result (identical, exit 0) the same shape as the thing being checked. The subset form is offered in both artefacts as a quoting escape hatch only.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix AC-4 and step 2 by scoping the right-hand extraction with hardcoded line numbers (`sed -n '380,549p'` on main's numbering) rather than by describe name.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works only before the change. This change inserts 14 lines above line 380, so the same command run after the change starts inside the comment block and ends 45 lines early. Any command that locates a describe by line number has to be written twice; matching on the name works once.

alternatives_considered.approach: Answer the last objection by keeping v4's qa_script step 3 exactly as written, including its trailing `grep -v` and its note that the pipeline exits 1 on success.

Collapsing it to one grep with exactly one expected hit, whose full text is given, removes the trap and makes the expectation sharper: it proves both that nothing else referenced the deleted file and that the survivor's only hit is the mandated comment.

That diff prints `10a11,23` plus 13 titles and exits 1 on a correct implementation, and the 13 belong to four describes out_of_scope forbids touching, so no conforming implementation could satisfy it. All three artefacts the objection names are fixed: AC-4.how_to_verify and qa_script step 2 now run one command that extracts the ten titles from main's file and the ten titles from the branch's two weekly describes and diffs them, expected result stated as the command can actually produce it — no output, exit 0; risks[0], which rested on the same unscoped comparison, now names the scoped command and records that the unscoped form was measured and fails. The reviewer's second option (a whole-file `comm -23` subset check) is offered only as a quoting escape hatch in both artefacts, because it is one-sided; the scoped diff is the check that runs. Applying the change in the working tree to run those commands for real, rather than reasoning about them, turned up three further defects in v4's own text, all now corrected: AC-2 claimed a 13-line added hunk where git counts 14 content lines (13 comments plus the blank separator); files[1] told the implementer to add a trailing blank without saying what the result looks like, and my own first insertion omitted it — files[1] and AC-2 now give the resulting layout as line numbers (378 `});`, 379 blank, 380-392 block, 393 blank, 394 `describe`); and qa_script step 3's trailing `grep -v` put the exit code on the second grep, which is a trap for a QA agent, so step 3 is now a single grep whose expected output is exactly one given line. The technical finding is unchanged and was re-measured from scratch: 76 changed lines in the describe-block diff, none containing an assertion; 7/3 split identical in both files; fixture md5-identical; the per-directory static test count 194 on main and 184 after. The v1 through v3 fixes are kept intact — the comparison lives in exactly one artefact, the release note is one sentence by repo convention, and files[1] quotes the comment verbatim so AC-2 and files[1] cannot disagree.
